nodes.label: Review severity scale A/B/C/D
nodes.rationale: A = shows wrong numbers or loses data (an engineer will decide on a lie); B = behaviour depends on how the operator reached that point, so the analysis is not reproducible; C = architectural debt that the next edit will break; D = performance, dead code, noise.

nodes.label: A1: SECTORS panel still computes sectors from the sample log
nodes.rationale: ProSectors calls zoneTimes(samples...) - the method LapTypes.h explicitly declares abandoned because log density depends on FPS and playback speed, part of the log belongs to an unplayed portion during replay, and with an incomplete log the sector boundary is not found at all. Timing moved to crossing-timestamp differences in RaceManager while SECTORS did not, so one screen holds two implementations of the same quantity.

nodes.label: A2: GPS fix type labelled against the protocol
nodes.rationale: Protocol.h says fix_type 4 = RTK_FIXED, but ProChannels maps 5 -> RTK Fixed and 4 -> RTK Float, so a real recording with fix=4 is displayed as Float. This is exactly the number that decides whether centimetre accuracy can be trusted, and there is currently no source of truth - the tracker firmware must arbitrate.

nodes.label: A3: telemetry export does not survive UTC midnight
nodes.rationale: time_s is computed as (utc_ms - first_utc_ms)/1000 while utc_ms counts milliseconds from midnight, so a session running 23:50 to 00:10 jumps -86400 s mid-file and the CSV time axis runs backwards. CsvImport already handles the midnight wrap explicitly - the same module, two different rules.

nodes.label: A4: CSV import time origin can stay zero
nodes.rationale: have_first_time is set even when to_number fails, so a corrupt time cell in the first coordinate row leaves first_time at zero and a SecondsFromStart recording is offset from zero instead of its real start.

nodes.label: B1: event log is built by observation, not from the recording
nodes.rationale: ProEvents keeps file-level statics (s_log, s_prev, s_sessBestLap, s_leader) and only creates an event when a rendered frame happens to catch the state change. Seek past a lap and its events never exist; open another recording and the old events remain because replay_close knows nothing about panels. This contradicts the very principle VehicleJournal was introduced for.

nodes.label: B2: TRACK REPORT and SECTORS ignore the operator-selected lap
nodes.rationale: ProTrackReport and ProSectors read v.m_current_lap_number (where the playhead sits) while GRAPHS and LAP LIST read Pro::AnalysisLap() (what the operator picked). Move the slider inside another lap and the screen shows two different laps at once with no sign they differ. Either every analysis panel follows AnalysisLap or none does.

nodes.label: B3: laps roll back on seek, sectors do not
nodes.rationale: restore_keyframe restores lap state from the snapshot but deliberately leaves sector state 'as played' (documented in ReplayPlayer.h). The consequence is the same as B1: sector times at the same point in the recording can differ from what the operator saw a minute ago, so the invariant 'one point in the recording, one picture' does not hold everywhere.

nodes.label: B4: one frame after a seek, position and timing disagree
nodes.rationale: main.cpp calls RaceManager::Update before replay_apply_pending_seek, so crossings queued in m_pending_crossings are parsed only by the next Update; during the seek only PublishPositionsOnly runs, leaving new positions with stale lap numbers, timers and table. One frame is small, but every derived 'car is on this lap' cue (LapTrace::at_playhead, LAP LIST row highlight) blinks in that window.

nodes.label: B5: panel state survives a change of recording
nodes.rationale: replay_close drops vehicles, session and device bindings but knows nothing about panel statics (s_analysis_lap, s_display_vehicle, s_view_min, s_view_span, s_log). The panels are not at fault: the replay module simply has no 'the recording changed' event for them to subscribe to.

nodes.label: C1: two locking idioms on one mutex
nodes.rationale: VehiclesLock is reentrant via a thread_local counter and supports a bulk section that the whole replay rollback rests on, yet ~20 sites take g_vehicles_mutex with a raw lock_guard. It works today only because both live on the render thread and never overlap; a single raw lock_guard added to the packet-ingest path would self-deadlock on the first rollback and present as a hang with no stack. A mutex that has a wrapper with semantics must never be taken bare.

nodes.label: C2: replay_journal returns a raw pointer into a mutating map
nodes.rationale: The pointer is valid 'until the replay closes' only because every participant currently lives on the render thread; g_journal.clear() in replay_close/build_journal would dangle every panel's pointer at once. A shared_ptr<const VehicleJournal> would cost one shared_ptr per frame and end the question.

nodes.label: C3: backward seek holds the vehicles mutex, forward seek does not
nodes.rationale: Backward rollback takes enter_vehicles_bulk_section so readers see only 'before' and 'after', but forward feed_range locks and unlocks per packet inside ingest, exposing thousands of intermediate states on a one-minute jump. The asymmetry is explained neither by a comment nor by the code - it is either intentional and undocumented, or an oversight.

nodes.label: C4: LapData::telemetryPoints is a dead field copied everywhere
nodes.rationale: The vector is never filled anywhere in the tree, yet LapData is copied into the snapshot every frame, into every keyframe, into the journal and into GetVehicleLapsCopy - each copy constructs and destroys an empty vector.

nodes.label: C5: sample rate declared in two places
nodes.rationale: RaceManager's kTelemetrySampleInterval = 0.1f and TelemetryExport's SAMPLE_RATE_HZ = 10.0 are unconnected; the second is written into the MoTeC CSV header, so changing the first makes the exported file lie silently. Only one side even carries a comment.

nodes.label: C6: journal warm-up blocks the frame with no sign of life
nodes.rationale: build_journal replays the entire recording synchronously on the render thread. Invisible on a 2.7 MB / 288 s file, but linear in length: an hour-long race with a full field freezes the window for seconds on open, with no progress indicator and no way to cancel - the only trace is a console line printed afterwards.

nodes.label: C7: journal duplicates vehicle history in memory
nodes.rationale: journal.lap_samples[lap] = session.samples copies every sample of every vehicle while Vehicle::laps still holds the live history, so replay telemetry sits in memory twice - roughly 2 x 21 MB for an hour with five cars now that LapInfo has grown to ~120 bytes. A side effect of snapshotting the journal by copy rather than a deliberate design.

nodes.label: D1: snapshot copies every lap of every vehicle each frame
nodes.rationale: PublishSnapshot assigns view.laps = vehicle.m_laps inside the loop over g_vehicles, on every Update and every seek step - a std::map with a node per lap and a vector inside each node, roughly 800 allocations per frame for values that have not changed since the last lap.

nodes.label: D2: LAP LIST copies the lap list and immediately discards it
nodes.rationale: GetVehicleLapsCopy is called and then overwritten by journal->lap_times; in replay - the panel's main mode - that first copy is never needed, and the journal check costs one map lookup and could come first.

nodes.label: D3: SECTORS scans all vehicles and all samples every frame
nodes.rationale: A loop over g_vehicles calling zoneTimes on each vehicle's best lap, under the vehicles mutex, every frame, with no cache; cost grows with both car count and lap length. It also binds auto& instead of const auto& on a read-only pass.

nodes.label: D4: dead constants in ProGraphs
nodes.rationale: CHANNEL_COUNT and MIN_SEEK_SECONDS are declared and used nowhere; MIN_SEEK_SECONDS even carries a three-line comment describing behaviour that does not exist in the code.

nodes.label: D5: settings written to disk on every wheel click
nodes.rationale: saveScales() and saveVis() open, rewrite and close pro_scales.ini directly in the input handler, so ten wheel clicks are ten file writes; a debounced or on-exit write is the obvious fix.

nodes.label: D6: CSV import holds the whole file as strings
nodes.rationale: CsvTable::rows is a vector<vector<string>> of every cell - 1.6 million std::string for an hour of 25 Hz logging. The binding dialog only needs column names and a dozen rows; the rest could be read in a second pass during conversion.

nodes.label: VehicleJournal (replay recording journal)
nodes.rationale: Exists precisely because a lap list that loses everything after the playhead is useless for post-race analysis; it holds the whole recording independent of where the operator has looked.

nodes.label: Pro::AnalysisLap (operator-selected lap)
nodes.rationale: The lap the operator explicitly chose, as opposed to m_current_lap_number where the playhead happens to sit; GRAPHS and LAP LIST follow it, the other analysis panels do not.

nodes.label: VehiclesLock (reentrant bulk-section lock)
nodes.rationale: Reentrant through a thread_local counter and offering enter_vehicles_bulk_section, so a reader waits and sees only the 'before' and 'after' of a rollback; freezing individual consumers pointwise did not solve that.

nodes.label: Invariant: timing anchored to source timestamps, not frames
nodes.rationale: Lap and sector times are computed from utc_elapsed_ms rather than deltaTime, which is exactly why a live session and its replay produce identical numbers; any edit that reintroduces deltaTime into time computation silently destroys this.

nodes.label: Invariant: one ingest path for all sources
nodes.rationale: Replay feeds ingest_wire_packet - the same entry point as the live receiver - so no second lap-counting implementation exists; that is the main reason the replay can be trusted. Foreign packets during replay are cut off at a single point rather than per source.

nodes.label: Invariant: keyframes without sample history
nodes.rationale: Snapshots exclude sample history, which makes them cheap enough for a 250 ms keyframe interval and near-instant rollback.

nodes.label: Invariant: panels read the published snapshot
nodes.rationale: Where implemented, panels read the published snapshot rather than live vehicles, so they cannot catch a half-finished rebuild.

nodes.label: Recommended fix order (A2, A1, A3/A4, B2, C1, B1/B5)
nodes.rationale: A2 first because it is cheapest and is lying right now about trust in the data; then A1 (a panel using an algorithm this same repo declares unfit); then the two silent-lie time bugs; then B2 to unify AnalysisLap usage; then C1 as protection against a hang that cannot be debugged; then a 'replay changed/seeked' event to replace immortal statics.
